title: Late Medieval Textuality and Poetic Authority
description: Authorship and poetic authority in Guillaume de Machaut, Christine de Pizan, Alain Chartier, Charles d'Orlans, and Franois Villon.

title: Representations of Medieval Gender
description: Representations of medieval gender.

title: Religion and Skepticism in Renaissance Europe
description: A study of the connections between religion and skepticism in a time of political and religious turmoil. Readings include works by Marguerite de Navarre, Rabelais, Machiavelli, Montaigne.

title: Renaissance Poetry
description: Renaissance poetry.

title: Irony in the Renaissance
description: Irony in the Renaissance.

title: Seventeenth and Eighteenth-Century Studies
description: Study of early modern French literature at a time of cultural and political transformation. Practice of theoretical approaches to early modern aesthetics, from Baroque and Classical theater and philosophy to Enlightenment fiction and epistemology.

title: Classical Tragedy
description: Study in depth of selected texts of the seventeenth century. B. Racine.

title: Classical Comedy
description: Study in depth of selected text of the seventeenth century. C. Moliere.

title: Les Moralistes
description: Study in depth of selected texts of the seventeenth century. F. Moralistes.

title: Topics in the French Classical Age
description: Study of the historical, intellectual, and cultural dimensions of France in the seventeenth century and/or the eighteenth century, with a focus on social institutions, literature, philosophy, religion and aesthetics. Emphasis on interdisciplinary methodology. Content varies.

title: The Libertine Novel
description: Exploration of the literary, philosophical, and aesthetic experimentations known as libertinage. In-depth study of various libertine novels, and their sexual and moral dimensions. Focus on the privileged spaces as well as the illustrations of libertinism.

title: Les Lumires: Fiction and Philosophy
description: What is Enlightenment in relation to the social institutions and the philosophical and religious traditions of the 18th century? Focus on the reinvention of nature, reason, passion, sentiment and morality in philosophical essays and new literary forms, including utopia.

title: Topics in Enlightenment Studies
description: Study of the Enlightenments central debates on education, religion, philosophy, and aesthetics, and of the main figures of the print and visual media, such as Chardin, Fragonard, Watteau, Grafigny, Montesquieu, Diderot, and Rousseau. Content varies.

title: Modern and Contemporary Studies
description: Close readings of nineteenth and twentieth-century literary texts; multi-disciplinary inquiry into the art and character of modernity. Practice of critical approaches for achieving an understanding of the literary, cultural, and social aspects of modernity and post-modernity.

title: Studies in the Novel
description: Close readings of nineteenth and twentieth-century literary texts; multi-disciplinary inquiry into the art and character of modernity. Practice of critical approaches for achieving an understanding of the literary, cultural, and social aspects of modernity and post-modernity.

title: The Theory of Fantastic Literature
description: Study of the current theories of fantastic literature and their limitations. Works by some of the following authors are examined: Cazotte, Nerval, Gauthier, Mrime, Nodier, Villiers, Maupassant, Apollinaire, Breton, Genet, Paulhan.

title: Topics in Modernism
description: Literary works read from various theoretical and cultural perspectives (psychoanalysis, feminism, cultural history, critical theory). Topics include: gender and sexuality in the novel, reading hysteria, the political unconscious, theorizing the gaze, Western representations of the Orient and the Other.

title: Modern and Contemporary Studies
description: Close readings of nineteenth and twentieth-century literary texts; multi-disciplinary inquiry into the art and character of modernity. Practice of critical approaches for achieving an understanding of the literary, cultural, and social aspects of modernity and post-modernity.

title: Post-colonial and Francophone Studies
description: Study of the literature and culture from French-speaking countries around the world, with emphasis on post-colonial politics and interactions between widely divergent cultural traditions. Theoretical examination of the epistemological issues raised by the introduction of non-Western perspectives.

title: Post-Colonial Francophone Narrative
description: An overview of La Francophonie du Sud. Emphasis on literary depictions of colonial history and its aftermath in texts from the Caribbean, West Africa, and the Maghreb.

title: Francophone Literature: The Caribbean
description: Readings from Haiti, Martinique, and Guadeloupe, with emphasis on the Creole oral tradition; slavery and the plantation system; race and multiculturalism; relations with France and the United States.

title: Francophone Literature: West Africa
description: Readings from the Congo, Zaire, Senegal, Cameroon, etc. Emphasis on the transition to independence; the oral tradition; social critique in film and the novel; the interaction of traditional beliefs with Islam and Christianity.

title: Francophone Literature: The Maghreb
description: Readings from Algeria, Morocco, and Tunisia. Emphasis on Islamic tradition; modernization; gender issues in Islam; contemporary political transformation.

title: Literature of Immigration and the Minority Experience
description: Study of the literary and cinematic currents reflecting the increasingly vital role played by immigrants and their descendents in the shaping of contemporary French culture. With an emphasis on the Beur phenomenon. Works by Sebbar, Begag, Beyala, Dridi, Allouache, among others.

title: Cultural Studies and Intellectual History
description: Analyses of literary, historical and philosophical readings that have shaped the ways in which French and European writers represent the human experience of time and space. Close look at the political, moral, and philosophical functions of art and literature.

title: The French Nation
description: Analyses of literary, historical and philosophical readings that have shaped the ways in which French and European writers represent the human experience of time and space. Close look at the political, moral, and philosophical functions of art and literature.

title: Game and Literature: historical, cultural and theoretical approaches

title: Modernity and the City
description: How was Paris deployed and dramatized, metamorphosed, and transfigured in the nineteenth century? Focus on panoramic literature, the invention of "the everyday" and of modern life, the expository spirit and world exhibitions, vision and spectatorship, commodities and consumer desires.

title: Literature and Travel
description: Analyses of literary, historical and philosophical readings that have shaped the ways in which French and European writers represent the human experience of time and space. Close look at the political, moral, and philosophical functions of art and literature.
